name: Trivia Bluff
description: Each round shows a real fact with one word missing. Students write a fake answer that sounds true, then everyone tries to pick the real one. Points for finding it and for fooling classmates.
when: When the class is flat and you want a bluffing game that teaches the facts on the way.

questions.question: The Roman emperor Augustus prohibited serving legionaries from ___, a decree that stayed in force for two centuries.
Because of their size, the males of the African driver ant are called "___".
In 1885 the German writer Heinrich Böhnke-Reich warned against using old ___ as coffee filters.

intro.message:
TRIVIA BLUFF!

You'll see an obscure fact with a blank. Write a believable lie to fill it in. The class will then try to spot the truth, but your lie might fool them!

qshow1.message:
Round 1 of 3

The Roman emperor Augustus prohibited serving legionaries from ___, a decree that stayed in force for two centuries.

Write your most believable lie!

qlies1.prompt:
The Roman emperor Augustus prohibited serving legionaries from ___, a decree that stayed in force for two centuries.

Write a lie that could fool the class.

qvote1.prompt:
Which one is the TRUTH?

The Roman emperor Augustus prohibited serving legionaries from ___, a decree that stayed in force for two centuries.

qreveal1.message:
The truth was: marrying!

recommendedFor: Older students who can write convincingly. Customize it down to one round for a quick warm-up.
